how_read: Each page was read with scripts/kb/fetch_wiki_live_pages.py's own code (its text extractor and page lookup), through a small wrapper (.scratch/fetch_wrap.py in the helper's copy, not committed) that asks for the page's current text by page name, because the Super Mario Wiki refuses the reader's request by revision id (HTTP 403). The revision named is the one the page lookup returned; the wrapper checked it equalled the revision of the text it parsed. Fetched pages are kept in build/wiki-live/mariowiki/. Every quoted sentence was checked, by script, to appear word for word in the page text read. Every page here also covers other Mario Party games: a line states a Mario Party 7 fact only where the page says so for Mario Party 7 (or gives the Mario Party 6 and Mario Party 7 fact together).
conflicts: Toady Orb: the Mario Party 7 page and the Toady Orb page say Toady throws away a green or blue Orb it takes, while the Toady page says it keeps the Orb for itself. No note here states what Toady does with a taken Orb.

lines.line: Summary: Landing on one of these spaces brings out a Koopa Kid, who then does one of several nasty things to you or to everyone. Mario Party 7 lets only Bowser and Koopa Kid make them.

quoted: spaces that generally summon a Koopa Kid when landed upon
In Mario Party 7, these spaces can only be created by Bowser and Koopa Kid, and appear wherever they randomly toss a Koopa Kid Orb.
Whenever someone lands on one, Koopa Kid will appear and do one of the following to his target:
Redistribute everyone's coins evenly, like a Bowser Revolution.
Shuffle everyone's Orbs.

lines.line: Weak points: It goes away if a different Orb is put on its square, if Yoshi and Birdo's Egg Orb is used on it, or if the Star Space moves onto that square.

quoted: by placing different Orbs in their location, destroying them with Yoshi and Birdo's Egg Orb
A Star Space may also occupy it.
The only ways to get rid of a Koopa Kid Space are placing a Character Space on it, using an Egg Orb or if the Koopa Kid space has the Star Space go to said space's location.

lines.line: Looks like: A round green space with a gold border and a gold Koopa Kid face in the middle.

quoted: They are round green spaces, with the Koopa Kid's face in gold at their center and a golden frame around them.

lines.line: Tips: His possible tricks: a Cursed Mushroom that limits your next roll to 1 to 5, an even split of everyone's coins, a roulette to swap coins or positions with one other player, a shuffle that moves every player, or a shuffle of everyone's Orbs. In Party Cruise Bowser scatters three Koopa Kid Orbs on the board at the start, and more get tossed when someone gets one from an Orb Space or is forced to buy one in Bowser's shop; Koopa Kid uses it at once.

quoted: Give the player a Cursed Mushroom, letting them roll only 1-5 on their next turn.
Redistribute everyone's coins evenly, like a Bowser Revolution.
Make the player swap coins with someone via the roulette wheel.
Use the Bowser Pipe, a specially designed Warp Pipe, to switch the player's position with one other player via the roulette.
Make everyone switch places with one another, like a Bowser Shuffle.
Shuffle everyone's Orbs.
The game always starts with Bowser tossing three Koopa Kid Orbs somewhere on the board
Getting a Koopa Kid Orb from an Orb Space, which Koopa Kid uses immediately.
Being forced to buy a Koopa Kid Orb from Bowser's Shop, which Koopa Kid then uses.
Bowser does not scatter three Koopa Kid Orbs across the board.

lines.line: Summary: On Pyramid Park in Party Cruise you take Stars from your rivals by paying for a Chain Chomp ride. The Chain Chomps are found in the board's pyramid doghouses.

quoted: players have to use Chain Chomps – found in pyramid dog houses – to steal Stars from opponents.
Party Cruise: Players need to pay to ride on Chain Chomps to steal Stars from their opponents.

lines.line: Weak points: Only this board has the Snack Orb; it guards you against Chain Chomps for three turns, ending early if one attacks.

quoted: In Mario Party 7, the Snack Orb is only found on Pyramid Park
After using a Snack Orb, the player is protected for three turns or until a Chain Chomp attacks

lines.line: Looks like: Most of the Chain Chomps are black, and one red Chain Chomp stands at the top left of the board; it is the one that gives three Dice Blocks.

quoted: a Red Chomp on the left side located at the top
the black Chain Chomps only offer one or two Dice Block roll at the same respective prices, while a Red Chain Chomp cost ten coins for three rolls.

lines.line: Tips: A black Chomp charges 10 coins per single Dice Block, or 20 for a pair; the red one charges 10 for three. In the final four turns every price is halved. Rolling matching numbers while riding earns no bonus coins.

quoted: let players ride on them for a price of 10 coins for one Dice Block (5 coins in the last four turns) or 20 for two (10 in the last four turns)
lets players use three Dice Blocks for ten coins (five coins in the last four turns)
Player do not get bonus coins if numbers on the Dice Blocks match while riding Chain Chomp.

lines.line: Summary: A statue on the left-hand side of Pyramid Park, towards the middle. Stepping on the Green Space before it wakes it, and it takes the visitor for a treasure thief and curses all players with one of three effects picked at random.

quoted: The Bowser Sphinx is located at the center left of Pyramid Park
When a character lands on the Green Space in front of the Bowser Sphinx, the sphinx awakens and assumes they are attempting to steal its treasure.
it curses the player, resulting in one of three random effects occurring, all of which apply to all players:

lines.line: Weak points: In Party Cruise the curse is triggered by the Green Space that faces the sphinx, so steer clear of that square to avoid it.

quoted: Stepping on the Green Space in front of the Bowser Sphinx awakens it, then it accuses the player of trying to steal its treasure.

lines.line: Looks like: A sphinx based on the Great Sphinx of Giza but with Bowser's head, crowned with a nemes whose lappets are striped pink and blue and which carries a Chain Chomp decoration.

quoted: Its body is modeled after the Great Sphinx of Giza, while its head resembles Bowser's, wearing a nemes with pink-and-blue striped lappets and a Chain Chomp ornament.

lines.line: Tips: The curse hits every player and is one of three: all coins are pooled and split evenly, every Blue Space turns Red and every Red Space turns Blue for two turns, or Chain Chomp rides are half price for two turns. A Whomp stands on the route to the Bowser Sphinx and wants 10 coins to let you through.

quoted: All players' coins are added up, then distributed evenly (equivalent to a Bowser Revolution).
All Blue Spaces become Red Spaces, and vice versa, for two turns.
All Chain Chomp rides cost half as many coins for two turns.
blocking the path to the Bowser Sphinx unless the player pays them ten coins.

lines.line: Summary: A black Star that sits in one of the treasure chests; opening it costs you one Star. On Grand Canal in Party Cruise, one of the four chests Blooper juggles holds it; in Solo Cruise the chests hold five coins and three Dark Stars.

quoted: are black Stars that appear in the Mario Party series
Dark Stars still have the same effect in Mario Party 7. At one of the Green Spaces in Grand Canal, the player must choose a chest from a group after the chests have been shuffled by a Blooper.

The Green Space in front of the juggling Blooper activates a guessing game, where Blooper juggles four chests that have: a Star, five coins, a Dark Star, and nothing (in Solo Cruise, there are always five coins, but three Dark Stars).
the player opening the chest with the Dark Star loses one Star.

lines.line: Tips: Once you pick the Dark Star's chest, you cannot refuse what is inside. On Neon Heights in Party Cruise, a Bowser Time event can drop a Dark Star into the chest that held the Bob-omb; pay Koopa Kid to open it and you are stuck with the Dark Star and lose one Star. If the chest with the ordinary Star gets opened first, the Dark Star vanishes. With no Stars you lose nothing here, whereas Mario Party 6 took 20 coins.

quoted: It happens exclusively in the Party Cruise.
Puts a Dark Star in the chest containing a Bob-omb, and the player opening the chest with the Dark Star loses one Star.
If the chest containing the Star is opened before this chest, the Dark Star disappears.
If the player chooses this chest, they must take it.
If the player pays Koopa Kid for this chest, they are forced to take the Dark Star inside.
Unlike in Mario Party 6, if the player has no Stars, they do not lose 20 coins.

lines.line: Summary: A boss minigame in which you ride an elevator while Bowser keeps attacking you; the goal is the 100th floor. Only Solo Cruise unlocks it, and it is the sole minigame with that limit.

quoted: Boss minigame
The objective of the minigame is to make it to the 100th floor while avoiding Bowser, who attacks the player.
It is the only minigame that is unlockable only in the Solo Cruise

lines.line: Weak points: Reaching floor 100 wins, even with Dice Block numbers still unused; a single hit from any attack loses the game on the spot.

quoted: The player wins if the 100th floor is reached, even if there are additional numbers remaining on the Dice Blocks.
The player automatically loses if they get hit by any of Bowser's or the Koopa Kid's attacks.

lines.line: Tips: Each turn you have four Dice Blocks to strike, and the climb equals their sum, from 4 up to 40 floors. Past floor 50 a Koopa Kid joins in, with the same attacks as Bowser (a trio of fireballs or a trio of missiles) plus a laser team attack. Solo Cruise records the floor you lost on, so you can continue from it. The minigame is called Bowser's Lovely Lift!

quoted: To beat this minigame, the player must hit four Dice Blocks, and the elevator goes up a number of floors based on the total roll.
The minimum number of floors the player can progress on one turn is four, and the maximum is 40.
After the 50th floor, a Koopa Kid appears and assists Bowser in attacking. They can perform a team attack with laser beams.
Individually, the Koopa Kid has the exact same attacks as Bowser: shooting three fireballs or three missiles.
in the Solo Cruise, the game tracks the floor the player lost on, and allows them (or the opponent) to resume the minigame from that point
Bowser's Lovely Lift! is a boss minigame in Mario Party 7.

lines.line: Summary: A yellow Thrown Orb you set on a space as a trap. When a rival stops on it, a Hammer Bro takes ten coins from them, and you receive the coins.

quoted: Thrown Orbs are traps that can be throw on a space.
The Thrown Orbs' shell color is yellow.
Opponents that land on a space containing the orb lose ten coins to the Hammer Bro, like the Spiny Orb in Mario Party 6.
the coins are given to the player that placed the Orb.

lines.line: Uses: Place it on a Blue, Red, Character or Koopa Kid Space. Every board has it apart from Pyramid Park and Bowser's Enchanted Inferno!

quoted: Orbs can be set only in Blue, Red, Character (not Roadblock), or Koopa Kid Spaces.
All boards except Pyramid Park and Bowser's Enchanted Inferno!

lines.line: Tips: It never hits its owner, and landing on your own Orb's space pays you five coins. A rival under a Metal Mushroom Orb ignores traps.

quoted: so the Hammer Bro Orb cannot affect the user.
If the owner lands on the space, they will receive five coins.
making them invulnerable to Trap Orbs put on spaces.

lines.line: Summary: A yellow Thrown Orb trap: a Piranha Plant chews up any rival who stops on it, and that rival loses half their coins to you.

quoted: The Thrown Orbs' shell color is yellow.
Opponents that land on a space containing the Orb are still eaten by a Piranha Plant and lose half their coins, which are then transferred to the space's owner.

lines.line: Uses: Set it on a space as a trap. The Orb Shop charges fifteen coins, and the only boards without it are Pagoda Peak and Windmillville.

quoted: it becomes the Piranha Plant Orb that players can only place on a space; it costs fifteen coins at the Orb Shop.
All boards except Pagoda Peak and Windmillville

lines.line: Tips: If you are already on the space when a rival arrives, the plant chews the rival only. Landing on your own trap gives you five coins.

quoted: If a player is already on the space of this orb, and another opponent lands on it, the Piranha Plant chews only the opponent, while the original player gets surprised.
If the owner lands on the space, they will receive five coins.

lines.line: Summary: A yellow Thrown Orb trap: a Spear Guy robs any rival who stops on it, taking as many coins as a Dice Block roll shows, and hands them to you.

quoted: The Thrown Orbs' shell color is yellow.
If a player who is not the owner of the space steps on it, a Spear Guy appears and steals an amount of coins determined by a Dice Block from the one who has stepped on the space.
The Spear Guy then gives the coins to the space's owner.

lines.line: Uses: Set it on any space you choose as a trap. It is on every board but Grand Canal and Neon Heights.

quoted: The Spear Guy Orb can be placed on a chosen space on the board.
All boards except Grand Canal and Neon Heights

lines.line: Tips: The Dice Block shows 5, 10, 20 or 30 coins. It takes the place of Mario Party 6's Goomba Orb.

quoted: The Dice Block can roll a 5, 10, 20, or 30.
This orb is the replacement for the Goomba Orb from Mario Party 6.

lines.line: Summary: A yellow Thrown Orb trap: Pink Boo robs a rival who stops on it of a Star, or of 20 coins if they hold none, and passes the loot to you.

quoted: The Thrown Orbs' shell color is yellow.
Any opponents who land on it will cause Pink Boo to appear and relieve them of a Star, or 20 coins if the opponent has none, and give whichever of them he got to whoever planted the trap.

lines.line: Uses: Set it on a space as a trap. Pagoda Peak and Windmillville are the only boards without it. Most shops ask 30 coins, and 15 when there is a discount.

quoted: All boards except Pagoda Peak and Windmillville
Most shops sell Pink Boo Orbs for 30 coins, or 15 if there is a discount.

lines.line: Tips: The trap turns the space into a Character Space, and Pink Boo shows up when a rival stops there. If you land on your own trap you get five coins.

quoted: they now appear when an opponent lands on a Character Space created by a Pink Boo Orb.
If the owner lands on the space, they will receive five coins.

lines.line: Summary: A yellow Thrown Orb trap: when a rival stops on it, Kamek turns up and hands you control of as many as three of that rival's Character Spaces.

quoted: The Thrown Orbs' shell color is yellow.

Opponents that land on a space containing the Orb summon Kamek, who uses his magic to give control of one of the Character Spaces they placed on the board to the owner of that space (three in Mario Party 7).

lines.line: Uses: Set it on a space as a trap. It costs ten coins in the Orb Shop, and only Pagoda Peak, Pyramid Park and Windmillville have it.

quoted: It costs ten coins at the Orb Shop.
Pagoda Peak, Pyramid Park, and Windmillville

lines.line: Tips: Kamek seizes the Character Spaces the victim had put on the board, and Mario Party 7 caps it at three. Landing on your own Thrown Orb space earns you five coins.

quoted: give control of one of the Character Spaces they placed on the board to the owner of that space (three in Mario Party 7).
If the owner lands on the space, they will receive five coins.

lines.line: Summary: A red Roadblock Orb with an Amp inside it. It affects any rival who moves over the space, not only one who stops there: the Amp shocks them, and they lose three coins for each space they move beyond it.

quoted: Roadblock Orbs are orbs with red shells and can be thrown on spaces.
It contains an Amp.
Opponents that pass through a space containing the orb get shocked by the Amp
In Mario Party 7, it serves the same purpose, but opponents lose only three coins per space, instead of five.
Roadblocks affect any player who passes by the space (not just those who land on it)

lines.line: Uses: Put it on a space as a roadblock. An Orb hut sells it for 15 coins, and Pagoda Peak, Neon Heights and Windmillville are where it appears.

quoted: It costs 15 coins at an Orb hut, and can be obtained on Pagoda Peak, Neon Heights, and Windmillville.
Pagoda Peak, Neon Heights, and Windmillville

lines.line: Tips: The shock is immediate, afterwards the space returns to normal, and roadblocks you placed never hurt you. A player who passes a second Zap Orb while the first is still draining coins gets both effects stacked, and the draining ends if their coins run out.

quoted: the effects occur immediately, though, unlike other Character Spaces, the space will revert to normal after activating once. Players are immune to the effects of Roadblocks they place.
In both games, if a player passes by another Zap Orb while one is already in effect, the Zap Orbs stack up. If the player runs out of coins, the effect wears off.

lines.line: Summary: A red Roadblock Orb. A rival who moves over the space is squashed by a Thwomp and cannot go further, so their turn ends there.

quoted: Roadblock Orbs are orbs with red shells and can be thrown on spaces.
Opponents that pass a space containing the Orb get flattened by a Thwomp, ending their turn.

lines.line: Uses: Put it on a space as a roadblock. Windmillville, Neon Heights and Pyramid Park are the boards that carry it.

quoted: In Mario Party 7, it can be obtained on Pyramid Park, Neon Heights, and Windmillville.
Pyramid Park, Neon Heights, and Windmillville

lines.line: Tips: Metal Mushroom protects a rival: the Thwomp bounces off and the roadblock achieves nothing. Once someone triggers a roadblock it is gone.

quoted: the Thwomp will attempt to crush that player, but it will be deflected, negating the roadblock.
They are triggered when an opponent passes them and disappear once triggered.

lines.line: Summary: A green Self Orb that turns you to metal so that the Trap Orbs rivals leave on spaces cannot harm you.

quoted: Self Orbs have a green shell and are used on the player.
A Metal Mushroom Orb has the effect of turning the user metal, making them invulnerable to Trap Orbs put on spaces.

lines.line: Uses: Use it on yourself for protection against rivals' traps. It appears on Windmillville, Pagoda Peak and Bowser's Enchanted Inferno!, costing anywhere between 5 and 30 coins.

quoted: Pagoda Peak, Windmillville, and Bowser's Enchanted Inferno!
The cost of a Metal Mushroom Orb in Mario Party 7 ranges from five to thirty coins.

lines.line: Tips: As metal you shrug off a Thwomp Orb (it bounces off), kick a Bob-omb Orb away, and watch a Tweester Orb fade out harmlessly.

quoted: the Thwomp will attempt to crush that player, but it will be deflected, negating the roadblock.
Like Mario Party 6, players kick away the Bob-omb when under the effect of a Metal Mushroom Orb.
If a player is under the effect of the Metal Mushroom Orb, the Tweester still tries to blow away that player, but it dissipates shortly after with no effect.

lines.line: Summary: A green Self Orb that only Pyramid Park has: use it on yourself, and a bone you throw keeps Chain Chomps off you.

quoted: Self Orbs have a green shell and are used on the player.
In Mario Party 7, the Snack Orb is only found on Pyramid Park
It serves to protect the player from Chain Chomp, which it does by allowing the player to throw the bone inside the Snack Orb to lead Chain Chomp astray.

lines.line: Uses: Use it on yourself before a Chain Chomp comes for you. It lasts three turns, or ends sooner if a Chain Chomp attacks, in which case the bone is thrown for you automatically.

quoted: The player now has to use it on themselves before they are attacked by Chain Chomp
After using a Snack Orb, the player is protected for three turns or until a Chain Chomp attacks, the latter of which prompts the automatic bone throw.

lines.line: Tips: Anyone else on your space is also safe. In real play the shield covers only two rounds of your rivals' turns: the count drops once you have moved through a Dice Block, yet rivals can use Chain Chomps only in the gaps between your turns.

quoted: It still also prevents other players on the same space as the user from being hit.

Since turns count down after the player moves through a Dice Block but opponents can only use Chain Chomps between the turns of the user, while the effect of the Snack Orb mechanically lasts for three turns in practice, it only protects the player from opponents's attacks for two of their turn cycles.

lines.line: Summary: A green Self Orb that makes the Dice Block crawl, letting you choose your roll.

quoted: Self Orbs have a green shell and are used on the player.
the Slow 'Shroom Orb slows down the speed of the Dice Block tremendously
allowing players to choose any number to roll.
Since the Slow 'Shroom Orb essentially allows the player to choose the number that they would like to roll

lines.line: Uses: Use it on yourself, then press the button while the number one step before your target shows. Every board carries it besides Pagoda Peak and Pyramid Park.

quoted: Players do this by hitting when the number that precedes the desired outcome is shown on the Dice Block.
All boards except Pagoda Peak and Pyramid Park

lines.line: Tips: The Dice Block counts upward and starts over after 10. To roll a three, for example, press the button as it shows a two.

quoted: rolls the numbers in ascending order and resetting after 10
For example, if a player wants to get a three, then the player hits when the Dice Block shows a two.
